title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM-Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics using the declared model "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20); we report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, run-accounting diagnostics, artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational deployment requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow ordering, and higher-order safety/policy constraints. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports advocate such workflow-centred mitigations [1]–[3], but provide limited large-scale paired measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed execution. Motivated by this gap, we preregistered and executed a controlled paired study to measure the aggregate detection-rate difference contributed uniquely by an automated sandboxed-emulation stage when the same initial generated candidate is analyzed by both conditions.

Research question and contributions. Our preregistered research question was: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete accounting; (3) an artifact-grounded interpretation explaining a near-zero marginal effect; (4) concise reproducibility pointers into the archived bundle and prescriptive boundary conditions where guarded stages are likely to matter.
sections.related_work: Prior survey and system reports document the practical trend of combining LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops to raise operational assurance for NetOps artifacts [1]–[3]. These works emphasize that correctness in intent→configuration pipelines is multidimensional: syntactic parsing, command-ordering/workflow constraints, invariants (e.g., keep‑one‑uplink‑up), and dynamic runtime properties may each require different V&V primitives. Tool-focused case studies (e.g., the evolution of Batfish and multimodal co-pilot prototypes) highlight both the power and limits of static analyzers and motivate layered validator+emulator designs that can reveal runtime semantics and side effects not captured by static rule sets [2], [3]. Our study is positioned as an artifact-grounded, preregistered, paired quantification of the marginal guarded-stage contribution under shared_initial_candidate sampling semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistered sample plan targeted Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440) with a minimum effect-of-interest of 0.20 for power planning. Inclusion/exclusion, missingness handling (deterministic reseed up to two times), multiplicity handling, and contamination controls were fixed in the preregistration.

Task generation and topology templates. Confirmatory items were generated deterministically from an intent_configuration_repair task family and cover three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit intent, required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break). Inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; no irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred and complete_pair_count = 720.

Model, sampling semantics, and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses). For each pair the run obtained exactly one sampled initial candidate and that identical candidate was presented to both downstream conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). This isolates downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation observations or permitted repair invocations) by removing generation variability as a source of between-condition discordance.

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) applies deterministic, rule-based checks: vendor-CLI parsing, per-command canonicalization, sequence-order enforcement, atomicity/workflow constraints, protected-interface invariants, group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance. The guarded pipeline runs the baseline validator and then executes the candidate in a sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and runs normalized CLI commands; emulation observations are translated into runtime-observation rules that can trigger additional detections not captured by the static validator.

Provider-call audit fields: interpretation and reconciliation. Reviewer concerns about audit-field asymmetry were addressed by inspecting the archived provider-call audit. Provider-call accounting reports the total hosted_model_call_event_count (721) and a stage_counts map with keys such as shared_initial_generation and repair. In our execution: shared_initial_generation = 720 (one model call per paired task to produce the shared sampled candidate) and repair = 1 (a single repair-stage model invocation occurred across the entire confirmatory set). condition_counts reported in the audit are counts of model calls made in condition-specific stages (e.g., the guarded-stage repair invocation) rather than counts of paired episodes; hence they can be numerically asymmetric even when complete_pair_count = 720. In short: (a) shared_initial_generation counts one model call per pair (720); (b) the single repair call appears under guarded-stage counts (1) because only one pair triggered the repair path; and (c) total model_calls_used = 721 reconciles these stage-level counts. These mappings are traceable in the archived reconciliation artifacts and are the basis for the run accounting reported in Results.

Analysis procedures. The pre-registered primary analysis used a paired-binary executor (McNemar-style exact test) with a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). The primary plan used complete-pair handling (no irrecoverable pairs present). Secondary per-class and per-vendor analyses were pre-specified as exploratory with Bonferroni-adjusted intervals.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and test statistics (artifact-grounded). Contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric values are taken directly from the archived analysis artifacts.

Discordant-pair attribution (artifact-grounded). The run accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. The single guarded-only discordant pair is pair-000504; in the archived summary this pair’s baseline episode failed validation while the guarded episode succeeded after the guarded-stage path that included the single recorded repair-stage invocation (transformation_id generate_validate_repair_v1). This mapping is preserved in the archived reconciliation and raw-results records and explains why stage-level condition_counts differ from episode counts even though complete_pair_count = 720.

Representative diagnostics and difficulty composition. Representative per-episode validator_trace objects show that most shared_initial candidates satisfied the validator rule set (violation_count = 0). The preregistered difficulty composition for the confirmatory bank was: extreme = 90 (12.5%), hard = 180 (25.0%), medium = 90 (12.5%), very_hard = 360 (50.0%). These counts are recorded in the archived difficulty summary and provide context for external-validity judgments.
sections.discussion: Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The archived evidence supports three artifact-grounded factors: (1) validator ceiling effect and task-rule alignment — the deterministic validator encoded the workflow constraints exercised by the curated tasks and left little headroom for additional guarded detections; (2) curated inclusion and reduced adversarial exposure — parser-validated, deterministically generated tasks underrepresent adversarial or noisy inputs where emulation commonly adds coverage; (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity — only one repair-stage call occurred, and the single guarded-only detection corresponds to that unique downstream event. Operational implication: when a high-coverage static validator is paired with a tightly curated input pipeline, automated sandboxed emulation may yield negligible incremental detection at scale. This conclusion is narrowly scoped to the preregistered regime; it does not imply guarded stages are unnecessary in adversarial, production-like, or more diverse settings. Follow-up work should target adversarial task banks, broader vendor diversity, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages add operational value.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection (pair-000504); because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, archived per-episode traces permit independent verification of that mapping. We interpret the result as arising from validator ceiling effects and curated task design; follow-up work should focus on adversarial and production-like task banks, multi-validator ensembles, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages add substantive operational value. The archived execution and analysis artifacts cited in the paper provide the canonical bundle for independent verification.

Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration id: f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e (preregistration frozen before execution). Initial master-prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution accounting (artifact-grounded): completed_episode_count = 1440, complete_pair_count = 720, model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock. The archived execution manifest is the canonical reproducibility bundle for per-file provenance and run artifacts.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.
Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the archived reconciliation artifacts.
